accuracy.evidence: Checked against EYFS Development Matters (2023) PSED and the ELGs Building Relationships and Managing Self (children at 4 to 5 apologise with adult support and begin to repair), DfE Relationships Education (2019) 'Respectful relationships' and 'Caring friendships' (friendships have ups and downs that can be repaired), and restorative-practice guidance that an apology names the harm and offers amends. The lesson never says a sorry must be forced or that every apology has to be accepted; the adult text warns against a forced sorry.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years beliefs: an accident needs no sorry (Who got hurt? prediction, acc tag, p3, m6), saying the word fixes everything (Help fix it prediction, run tag, m8 'shouts sorry and runs off'), sorry while keeping the toy (keep tag, m1), a fib to dodge blame (fib tag, 'The cup did it'), and needing many sorries or staying cross for ever (more and ever tags in Friends again, m3).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsorry is built on repair: each harm has its own fix-it (blocks rebuild the scattered tower, the teddy returns, a plaster for the knee, kind words, a cloth, tape), and the hurt child's face and heart only fill when the matching repair lands. flagfriend sorts friendship qualities and orders calm-sorry-play; flagcare matches kind acts to strangers. The shingle gate shows 5% similarity with flagfriend, 4% with flagcare.

lab_teaches.evidence: After the good sorry Mia's face only moves from crying to sad and her heart is a third full, so the child sees that sorry alone is not enough; the heart only fills when the right fix-it is dropped on her. A wrong fix bounces with 'Give it back? Mia needs the tower built again', so matching the repair to the harm is discovered by trying. In the playground, tapping a happy child gives 'Nothing went wrong, so no sorry is needed', so the child learns to read faces for hurt, not for blame.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong answers that the next task disproves: 'Yes, sorry fixes it all' (Mia stays sad until the blocks go back) and 'No, it was an accident' (Zoe, bumped by mistake, is crying and needs a sorry). The done line quotes the child's own guess via A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge scenes with tagged wrong answers; why() returns a specific correction for each slip: run 'Sorry is a start, but help fix it too', acc 'A mistake can still hurt', keep 'Sorry is not enough if you keep it. Give it back', ever 'One fall-out is not for ever', fib, laugh, mean and none. Every wrong tap inside the lab also names the slip through SAYWHY or the NEED message.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK -1.1 against the family kid target of 5.0, in short concrete sentences ('Took a toy? Give it back.'). Adult text is FK 7.3 against 10.0 and uses the precise early-years terms: PSED, Early Learning Goals Building Relationships and Managing Self, make amends, restorative approach, intent, accept the apology, forgiveness.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed; explanation overlap with every other lesson is at most 0.3% (6-word shingles). Kid paragraphs cover the oops, the named sorry plus the repair, matching fixes to harms, and accepting a sorry; adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, the three-part apology model, four named mistakes with a caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for all six steps: the two faces, heart and scattered tower sit above three tall picture cards (plaster, teddy, blocks) with labels; the playground wraps to 3 + 2 cards under 520 px so faces stay large and captions readable; young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall and wrap without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five Show me tasks completed, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme, and no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button twin (each sorry, each fix-it 'Give: ...', each child 'Give a sorry to Zoe: ...', each make-up line), and the canvas aria-label is updated with every message.
